sections.html:
Slidell sits on the northeast shore of Lake Pontchartrain in St. Tammany Parish and belongs to the New Orleans metropolitan area. The 2020 census counted 28,781 residents. Interstates 10, 59 and 12 meet nearby, which makes it a commuter base for the region.

Most of what shapes a sale here is water. The land is low and flat, buyers and lenders ask about flood zones first, and old repairs or missing records can slow a conventional deal.

sections.h2: How flooding affects a Slidell house sale
sections.html:
The city's Flood Safety brochure names three sources of flooding: hurricane storm surge, back flooding of Bayou Bonfouca when Lake Pontchartrain is inundated, and local drainage problems during heavy storms. Flooding can happen in any season, and because so much of the land is low and flat, all properties are potentially at risk.

Hurricane Katrina is the reference point. The municipal area is about 2 miles inland, yet parts of the city saw storm surge above 10 feet on August 29, 2005. Unincorporated areas of St. Tammany to the south and east that often carry a Slidell address saw 13 to 16 feet.

Find the flood zone before you list. The city's Floodplain Administrator in the Building Safety Department can tell you, and can advise on whether a property is prone to flooding.

sections.h2: Permits and repairs before you sell
sections.html:
Slidell has a flood hazard prevention ordinance that meets National Flood Insurance Program standards. A permit is required for any development, a term that covers new construction, substantial improvements, demolitions and excavations. Anyone who fills, dumps or excavates land or drainage ways without permission can be ordered to restore it at their own cost.

  • Planning Department: 985-646-4320, at 250 Bouscaren St, Suite 203, Slidell, LA 70458.
  • Building Safety Department: 985-646-4323.
  • Engineering Department: 985-646-4270.
  • Code Enforcement: 985-646-6134.

Call before you pick up a hammer. Ask Building Safety whether your planned repairs count as a substantial improvement, and whether a drainage or fill change needs engineering review. Confirm these phone numbers with the city before you rely on them.

Insurance timing can decide whether a buyer can close on schedule. Standard property insurance does not cover surface flooding, so a separate National Flood Insurance Program policy is needed. New flood policies usually have a 30 day waiting period, and no new policy can start once a named storm has formed in or entered the Gulf of Mexico.

There is one break for buyers: if you buy a new home, the 30 day waiting period does not apply, and coverage starts once the application is approved after closing. You can help a buyer by having the property's flood zone and any prior claims ready early.

Repetitive loss means two or more NFIP claims over $1,000 each within a rolling ten years. Severe repetitive loss has stricter tests, and federal grants for these properties can pay for elevation, acquisition or demolition. If your house flooded more than once, ask the Finance Department about them.

sections.h2: Who collects property tax on a Slidell house
sections.html:
The St. Tammany Parish Sheriff does, for Slidell as well as the unincorporated parish. Under Louisiana law the sheriff in each parish collects property taxes, and the Property Tax Division handles Slidell, Mandeville, Covington, Abita Springs, Pearl River and Madisonville under separate contract.

Contact methodDetail
Phone985-809-8217

Slidell officeSheriff's Administrative Building, 300 Brownswitch Rd

Hours8:00 am to 4:30 pm, Monday to Friday
MailTax Collector, P.O. Box 1450, Covington, LA 70434

The division also issues property tax research certificates and handles redemptions of property sold at the annual tax sale. It is the place to ask whether a delinquent bill exists before a sale.

The St. Tammany Parish Clerk of Court records conveyance, mortgage and miscellaneous documents about immovable property for the entire parish, through its Recording Department. The clerk posts a 2026 fee schedule as a PDF, and the main number for the office is 985-809-8700.

Louisiana sales are passed before a notary. A title company or notary usually takes the signed act of sale to the clerk and pays the recording fee from closing funds.

sections.h2: What a Slidell seller must disclose
sections.html:
Louisiana law asks sellers of residential property to complete a property disclosure document. R.S. 9:3198 requires a form prescribed by the Louisiana Real Estate Commission, or one with at least its minimum language. With Slidell's flood history, that form is where past water damage and repairs belong.

Be specific. Write down what flooded, when, what was replaced and who did the work. Mold, old repairs and missing records are the items that stall a conventional sale, and they are one reason some owners look at a cash offer.

sections.h2: A step by step path to closing
sections.html:
Slidell sales move more smoothly when the water questions are answered before the first showing. Here is a workable order.

  1. Get the flood zone from the Floodplain Administrator and note whether the house has flooded before.
  2. Collect repair receipts, permits and any insurance claim records. If work was done without a permit, call Building Safety before a buyer finds out.
  3. Ask the Sheriff's Property Tax Division for a research certificate so you know whether any bill is delinquent.
  4. Fill in the Louisiana disclosure form honestly, with the flood history in it.
  5. Sign the act of sale before a notary. The notary or title company records it with the St. Tammany Clerk of Court and pays the fee from your proceeds.

Sellers who live out of the area can do most of this by phone and email with the offices listed above. A cash buyer shortens the middle of this list, because no lender is waiting on an appraisal or a repair list. The title, tax and recording steps do not go away. They only get done faster when the paperwork is ready.

sections.h2: When a cash sale fits a Slidell house
sections.html:
It tends to fit a house with flood damage that has not been repaired, a house with a lapsed flood policy, an estate property or a rental the owner no longer wants. A cash buyer takes the property as it stands, so a lender's appraisal and repair demands are not part of the deal. Title work, tax certificates and recording still apply.

Before you compare offers, line up the same short list for every route: the flood zone, any prior flood claims, repair receipts and permits, a tax status check with the Sheriff's division and a recorded-documents check with the clerk. Having those in hand lets a buyer price the house faster, whether that buyer is paying cash or using a loan.

faqs.q: Is Slidell in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of it are. The city says all properties are potentially at risk because the land is low and flat. Call the Floodplain Administrator in Building Safety at 985-646-4323 to learn a specific property's zone.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to repair a flooded house in Slidell?
faqs.a: Slidell requires a permit for any development, including substantial improvements and demolitions. Ask Building Safety before starting work.

faqs.q: Who do I pay Slidell property taxes to?
faqs.a: The St. Tammany Parish Sheriff's Property Tax Division collects them for Slidell under contract. You can call 985-809-8217.

faqs.q: Does a buyer get a flood insurance waiting period after buying in Slidell?
faqs.a: The 30 day waiting period does not apply when you buy a new home. Coverage starts after the application is approved following closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Slidell house with unrepaired storm damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Conventional buyers may ask for repairs or walk away, while a cash buyer can offer on the house as it stands. Clear title and tax status are still needed.
